script_nghe: Today, sleep. The commonly cited recommendation for adults is seven to nine hours; I’ll use seven as the lower bound. Around thirty-five per cent of adults in the surveyed countries report sleeping less than that. Now, the strongest and most consistent finding concerns cognitive performance — reaction time, attention, memory. The evidence on mood is reasonably good. The weakest evidence, and I want to be clear about this, concerns immune function; it’s frequently reported but the studies are small. Our own study followed four hundred and twenty participants. Your assignment on this is due on the twenty-second.

phan.noi_dung:
**LECTURE — SLEEP RESEARCH**

- Recommended sleep for adults: **1** ____________ hours
- Percentage sleeping less: about **2** ____________ %
- Strongest link found with: **3** ____________ performance
- Weakest evidence concerns: **4** ____________
- Study sample size: **5** ____________
- Assignment due: **6** ____________

> **Reading the small print of a study**
> 
> Newspaper reports of research follow a predictable shape. A finding is described in confident terms, a single figure is quoted, and a researcher is given a sentence expressing enthusiasm. What is almost always omitted is the qualifying language that appeared in the original paper.
> 
> Consider a typical example. A study reports that people who drink coffee show a lower rate of a particular illness. In the paper, the authors note that the association is modest, that it weakens when smoking is accounted for, that the participants were volunteers who may differ from the general population, and that no causal relationship can be established from observational data. By the time this reaches a headline, it has become the claim that coffee prevents the illness.
> 
> Some responsibility lies with journalists, but the pressure operates in both directions. University press offices compete for attention, and studies have found that exaggeration in news coverage frequently originates in the press release rather than the reporting. Where the release was measured, coverage was measured too.
> 
> Readers are not powerless. Three questions catch most overstatement: How large is the effect in absolute terms? Were the participants typical of the people the claim is about? And does the study observe or intervene? A finding that survives all three deserves attention. Most do not survive the first.

**True / False / Not Given (7–10):**
7. Newspaper reports usually include the qualifying language of the original paper.
8. Exaggeration often begins in university press releases.
9. Most journalists deliberately distort findings.
10. Where press releases were measured, coverage tended to be measured as well.

**Hoàn thành câu (11–14):**
11. The coffee association weakened when ____________ was accounted for.
12. Participants were ____________ who may differ from the general population.
13. No ____________ relationship can be established from observational data.
14. Most findings do not survive the ____________ question.

writing.de_tom_tat: Bài A — viết lại 3 câu bằng ngôn ngữ giảm nhẹ phù hợp văn học thuật.
writing.bai_mau:
CÂU 1 — Social media destroys teenagers' mental health.
  → Heavy use of social media may contribute to poorer mental health among some teenagers.
     [destroys → may contribute to · thêm Heavy use, some · thêm poorer thay vì tuyệt đối]

CÂU 2 — Everyone knows that exams are useless.
  → It is widely felt that examinations are of limited value as a measure of ability.
     [Everyone knows → It is widely felt · useless → of limited value · thêm phạm vi as a measure of ability]

CÂU 3 — Immigration always causes unemployment.
  → In certain circumstances, immigration may be associated with short-term pressure on local employment.
     [always → In certain circumstances, may · causes → be associated with · thêm short-term, local]

BỘ TỪ GIẢM NHẸ theo mức độ chắc chắn giảm dần:
  · is likely to · tends to · may well · appears to · may · could · in some cases
  · a majority of · many · some · a minority of
  · considerably · relatively · somewhat · slightly · marginally

cham_diem.tieu_chi: Dùng ngôn ngữ giảm nhẹ đúng (2đ)
cham_diem.vi_sao: Ba kỹ thuật xuất hiện ở mọi câu: động từ giảm chắc chắn (may contribute, may be associated) · giới hạn phạm vi (some teenagers, short-term, local, as a measure of ability) · bỏ từ tuyệt đối (destroys → contribute to, always → in certain circumstances).
Cả ba câu vẫn nêu đúng luận điểm gốc, chỉ bớt tính tuyệt đối. Giảm nhẹ không có nghĩa là làm câu trở nên vô nghĩa hay không có quan điểm.

dang_hoc:
Ba lớp giảm nhẹ, dùng kết hợp:
1. Động từ: causes → may contribute to · proves → suggests
2. Lượng: everyone → many · all → a majority of
3. Phạm vi: thêm in some cases · among certain groups · in the short term
Vì sao quan trọng: câu tuyệt đối rất dễ bị bác bỏ. "Social media destroys mental health" chỉ cần một phản ví dụ là sai. "May contribute to poorer mental health among some teenagers" thì khó bác.
Tránh hoàn toàn: always · never · everyone · nobody · all · totally · completely trong văn học thuật.
Nhưng đừng giảm nhẹ quá: "It might possibly perhaps be the case that…" là mất điểm, không phải được thêm.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Dùng always/never/everyone → dấu hiệu rõ nhất của bài band thấp.
❌ Giảm nhẹ chồng chất: "may possibly perhaps somewhat…" → chọn một mức là đủ.
❌ Giảm nhẹ đến mức không còn quan điểm → "Some people may think something" là câu vô nghĩa.
❌ Nhầm correlation với causation: "causes" phải đổi thành "is associated with" khi chỉ có tương quan.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 3 — dùng ngôn ngữ giảm nhẹ để trả lời câu hỏi khái quát.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Do young people today work harder than previous generations?
cau_tra_loi.mau: It's difficult to generalise. They tend to work longer hours, from what I've seen, though the nature of the work has changed — it's less physical but more constant. I'd hesitate to say one generation works harder than another.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "It's difficult to generalise" và "I'd hesitate to say" — hai cụm giảm nhẹ mở đầu và kết thúc. Vẫn có nội dung cụ thể ở giữa.

cau_tra_loi.mau: Up to a point, I'd say. Financial security appears to remove a great deal of stress, which certainly helps. Beyond a certain level, though, the relationship seems to weaken considerably.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "appears to", "seems to", "up to a point", "beyond a certain level" — giảm nhẹ đúng cách cho câu hỏi khái quát.

cau_tra_loi.mau: Some, almost certainly. Whether it's most is far less clear — previous waves of automation eliminated certain roles while creating others. I'd expect significant disruption rather than wholesale replacement.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "almost certainly" cho phần chắc chắn, "far less clear" cho phần không chắc. Phân biệt được hai mức là dấu hiệu band cao.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Trả lời có mức độ chắc chắn khác nhau cho từng phần, không tuyệt đối.
generalise · hesitate to say · up to a point · disruption · wholesale.
appears to · seems to · Whether it's most is far less clear…

meo_noi: Câu hỏi khái quát ở Part 3 luôn cần giảm nhẹ. Trả lời tuyệt đối là mất điểm ngay.
"It's difficult to generalise, though…" là mở đầu an toàn nhất — vừa giảm nhẹ vừa cho bạn thời gian nghĩ.
Phân biệt mức chắc chắn trong cùng câu trả lời ("almost certainly… far less clear") — kỹ thuật band 7+.
